entry.title: Perceptual Characterization of Scan-induced Artifacts in Dynamic 3D Meshes
entry.summary: Dynamic meshes reconstructed from real-world scenes often exhibit scan-induced artifacts such as surface jitter and missing geometry, which strongly impact perceived visual quality. Objective assessment remains challenging due to the absence of artifact-free ground truth and limited perceptual understanding of artifact interactions. This paper presents a systematic and controlled perceptual study of scan-induced artifacts in dynamic meshes, focusing on surface jitter and holes. To enable systematic analysis, we introduce a physically grounded artifact synthesis framework in which holes are synthesized using a reconstruction uncertainty model derived from multi-view geometry. The study reveals asymmetric cross-artifact interactions, non-additive integration, and motion-dependent temporal masking. Based on these findings, we propose a compact, perceptually grounded no-reference quality assessment framework that encodes the observed perceptual mechanisms.

entry.title: DoReMe: Dual optimization of Reconstruction and Motion estimation for self-navigated free-breathing abdominal MRI using Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: Purpose: Free-breathing abdominal MRI is limited by respiratory motion, which introduces image artifacts and k-space inconsistencies. Existing reconstruction approaches often depend on pre-estimated motion fields or external respiratory surrogate signals. We propose a coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm for self-navigated free-breathing acquisition, in which motion is represented by compact Gaussian primitives and jointly refined with the image estimates during iterative reconstruction. Methods: An iterative reconstruction that alternates between data consistency updates and motion modelling was proposed. Respiratory motion was represented using Gaussian primitives. A Gaussian splatting was integrated into the reconstruction algorithm. The method was evaluated on self-navigated free-breathing Cartesian gradient-echo (GRE) acquisition in four healthy volunteers, including retrospective scan shortening experiments, and was compared with regularized compressed sensing (CS) reconstruction. Results: Respiratory motion states were reconstructed in approximately 1.5 min. Compared with CS, the proposed method improved visual image quality, particularly in coronal liver views, and better preserved anatomical structures in retrospectively shortened acquisitions. These findings provide proof of concept for the proposed method. Conclusion: The proposed coupled reconstruction-motion estimation algorithm improved visual image quality compared with CS alone. Gaussian primitives provided a compact and sufficiently flexible representation of nonrigid respiratory motion with practical runtime, supporting further scanner integration and validation in larger cohorts.

entry.title: Focus, Align, and Diffuse: Time-Series-Aware Keyframe Diffusion for Cardiac Dynamic Synthesis from Sparse Observations
entry.summary: Dense cardiac dynamics are essential for assessing cardiac function, yet in practice clinicians often observe only extremely sparse measurements. However, recovering full dynamics from such sparsity is a highly ill-posed problem due to the lack of temporal cues. While auxiliary time-series signals like ECG provide physiological guidance, effectively exploiting them is challenging due to the cross-modal representation gap and phase misalignment. In this work, we present CardioFAD, a Focus--Align--Diffuse paradigm that reformulates sparse cardiac dynamic synthesis as a recoverability--alignability anchor discovery problem. Our core insight is that resolving extreme temporal ambiguity requires a compact set of anchor states that are both sufficient to recover the visual trajectory and reliable for ECG--visual alignment. We therefore learn motion-salient keyframes under two complementary principles: trajectory sufficiency, which preserves trajectory-critical intra-modal motion content, and anchor alignment, which promotes consistent inter-modal correspondence at these anchors. We implement the Focus and Align modules optimized by the two aspects. Diffuse then performs two-stage generation by first synthesizing keyframes and subsequently interpolating the remaining frames. Extensive experiments on cardiac MRI and echocardiography videos demonstrate superior visual quality, temporal coherence, and improved functional consistency under the extreme one-shot regime.

entry.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
entry.summary: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

entry.title: Augmenting Real-time Visualization in Minimally Invasive Surgery with Particle Filtering and Depth-Aware Occlusion Handling
entry.summary: We present a real-time, hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). Occlusions caused by surgical instruments often obscure the region of interest (ROI), affecting surgical precision. To address this, our approach integrates enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) based detection, Particle Filtering (PF), and monocular depth estimation using Multiple Depth Estimation Accuracy with Single Network (MiDaS). Occlusion is detected using a distance-based threshold between instruments and ROI. Experimental results demonstrate robust instrument detection with a confidence score of 0.85, effective occlusion event handling, and accurate depth prediction with an MAE of 0.34 cm and RMSE of 0.53 cm. Independent phantom-based validation against stereo depth measurements yielded an MAE of 0.65 cm and RMSE of 0.66 cm. The framework further achieved an occlusion detection accuracy of 81.95\% while maintaining real-time performance at 38.7 FPS. Preliminary surgeon feedback indicates that the proposed visualization framework is clinically relevant and holds promise for future intraoperative image-guided navigation and decision support in MIS.

entry.title: Recovery-Oriented Optical System Design Based on Fisher Information
entry.summary: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). Although these metrics effectively characterize direct imaging performance, they do not necessarily indicate optimal behavior when image restoration is subsequently applied. In modern imaging pipelines, however, optical systems are increasingly combined with physics-based or learning-based restoration methods, making the information transfer properties of the optical system critically important. In this work, we propose a recovery-oriented optical design approach that explicitly links optical system optimization with image restoration performance through an estimation-theoretic framework based on Fisher information. A new design criterion is adopted to ensure that the information encoded by the optical system can be reliably recovered during image restoration. To validate the proposed approach, two dual separated aspheric lenses are designed under identical configurations using conventional RMS-based optimization and the proposed recovery-oriented optimization, respectively. Although the RMS-optimized lens exhibits superior direct imaging quality, it underperforms after image restoration compared to the recovery-oriented design. These results demonstrate that recovery-oriented optical design provides a physically interpretable and effective extension of traditional optical design criteria for imaging systems operating within modern computational imaging pipelines.

entry.title: Personalising Deformable Image Registration with Clinical Context and Deformation History for Adaptive Radiotherapy
entry.summary: Adaptive radiotherapy must account for anatomical changes during treatment, but doing so depends on reliably mapping targets, organs at risk and dose across serial images. Existing registration methods treat each image pair independently, without using radiotherapy-specific context or the patient's preceding anatomical trajectory. We developed Clinical-context-Aware and Patient-adaptive Deformable Image Registration (CAP-DIR), integrating source contours, dose, clinical text and prior-registration features. We evaluated 16,361 CT examinations from 3,473 patients across four institutional cohorts and five public benchmarks. CAP-DIR increased internal-test organ-at-risk-region normalized cross-correlation from 84.76% to 96.92% relative to the strongest learning-based comparator, with low deformation folding, and remained superior across seven external cohorts. In a blinded review of 20 longitudinal cases, clinically acceptable contours increased from 45.0% to 82.5% for clinical target volumes and from 22.5% to 62.5% for organs at risk, while estimated editing time decreased. In a controlled benchmark, CAP-DIR reduced global dose-mapping error by 34.5% relative to the strongest comparator. These findings show that clinically informed, longitudinal registration can improve contour usability and dose mapping for adaptive radiotherapy.

entry.title: Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition for Building STRATA-S12: An Open SAR-Optical Corpus for Self-Supervised Learning
entry.summary: Building a co-registered SAR-optical corpus for self-supervised Earth Observation is above all an acquisition problem, yet the main multi-modal datasets are collected opportunistically, with no per-stratum quota control, so the regions and seasons that cloud cover hits hardest end up under-sampled. We present Deficit-Driven Stratified Acquisition (DDSA), an algorithm that casts the construction of a Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 corpus as a constrained maximum-coverage problem over a land-cover-driven, hemisphere-corrected (class x season x region) stratification of target countries on all six inhabited continents, and solves it online: acquisition is ordered by marginal gain against a per-stratum deficit that the quality gates and a visual review of every accepted pair keep updating during the run. Three results follow from measuring the algorithm on its own product. First, stratum balance is a property of the deficit-driven ordering rather than of run length: replayed over all 2,928,370 real acquisition attempts, failures included, it populates all 192 strata within 0.05% of the attempts, against 4.03% for uniform round-robin effort and 20.5% for a random order. Second, whether a rejected attempt can be recovered is better predicted by how long its cause persists than by the type of defect: cloud rejections are recovered at eta = 18.8% against 41.4% for nodata, consistent with clouds persisting through a season. Third, the repair loop supplies 39.5% of the released pairs at no measurable quality cost, with 89.8% surviving manual review, but it adds yield rather than balance. The quality guarantee has a price: 2,928,370 acquisition attempts produced 740,746 released pairs. We release the corpus, STRATA-S12, with per-pair metadata sidecars aligned with the STAC and PDS4 standards and the FAIR principles, and a pre-registered linear probe confirms it is fit for self-supervised pre-training.

entry.title: Low-Altitude Agentic Networks: From UAV Connectivity to Workflow-Driven Capability Orchestration
entry.summary: Low-altitude platforms are evolving from connected sensing nodes into autonomous agents capable of bounded task interpretation, skill invocation, and local decision making. Increasing the intelligence of individual unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), however, does not resolve the organization problem that arises when mission workflows depend on capabilities distributed across multiple platforms and provider feasibility changes with network, resource, and mobility conditions. We propose low-altitude agentic networking as a task-level networking paradigm and develop a reference architecture that separates workflow logic from executor identity. Within a validated domain-specific workflow space, each ready operation is translated into a capability requirement and dynamically bound to an agent that remains feasible under current conditions. Task contracts and structured evidence govern workflow execution, while routine provider and link changes are handled through workflow-preserving local adaptation before high-level repair is invoked. A trace-calibrated discrete-event case study identifies a bounded operating region: conventional organization remains effective for simple workflows under stable conditions, whereas agentic networking becomes beneficial when workflow dependencies are tightly coupled, capability feasibility changes during execution, and viable local recovery paths remain available.

entry.title: Background2Background: a self-supervised background removal framework for high dimensional microscopy
entry.summary: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. We present Background2Background (B2B), a self-supervised background removal framework leveraging the backgrounds larger correlation relative to the signal. Local pixel shuffling disrupts signal correlations while preserving background structure, transforming signals into effective noise for Noise2Noise-based background removal. Across fluorescence, stimulated Raman scattering and mid-infrared photothermal imaging, B2B achieves over 40-fold background suppression and reveals hidden signatures.

entry.title: Calibrating Generative Flows through Regional Probability Matching
entry.summary: Generative models offer a powerful route to scientific simulation and discovery by enabling the study of complex populations and rare phenomena. Flow matching can generate realistic samples, yet inaccurate occurrence frequencies can distort population statistics and compromise inferences about rare events. Here we developed generalized mass-preserving coupled flow matching (G-MPCF), which matches the probability masses of Gaussian source regions to those of weighted data regions. This construction encodes the desired regional frequencies in the correspondence between noise and observations, shaping the learned dynamics while preserving the prescribed target distribution. On a rare-mode benchmark, G-MPCF reduces relative score error by 95.0% and numerical integration error by 89.9% compared with independent flow matching. On CIFAR-10 with a 100:1 class-probability ratio, it reduces corrected class-mass error by 44.6% compared with minibatch optimal transport, while improving mean image fidelity with matched computational budgets. We envision that incorporating regional probability calibration into generative modelling will support more reliable scientific simulation and inference, enabling the study of systems in which rare events and their occurrence frequencies are central to understanding the underlying mechanisms.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Cortical Surface Reconstruction and Spherical Registration for Heterogeneous Brain MRI
entry.summary: Surface-based cortical analysis is useful in many applications as it is a natural way to model the highly folded structure of the cerebral cortex, allowing quantities such as curvature and thickness to be easily calculated. Existing deep learning (DL) methods have focused on 1x1x1 mm3 T1-weighted (T1w) scans, thus replicating classical pipelines. Here we present a neural network that is trained exclusively on synthetic scans with random contrast and resolution. Consequently, it can be applied to almost any kind of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan. In addition, our model provides vertex-wise uncertainty estimates of the predicted surface as well as a spherical registration to fsaverage space. Our model performs on par with other state-of-the-art DL methods on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans and outperforms the only other method capable of estimating cortical surfaces from low resolution, non-T1w scans. The predicted uncertainty, moreover, correlates with overall scan quality on low resolution scans and highlights areas of poor surface reconstruction on 1x1x1 mm3 T1w scans, suggesting that it can be used for quality control. Finally, the predicted spherical registrations prove comparable to other DL and classical registration methods. These qualities, when combined with the fast inference time, will provide the ability to analyze large, existing databases of clinical MRI scans, with the potential for finding disease-specific patterns that would otherwise be infeasible in a research setting.

entry.title: Hybrid Context Forests and Bilateral Viterbi Matching for 3D Rib Centerline Tracing in CT
entry.summary: Automatic extraction and anatomical numbering (R01-R12, L01-L12) of all 24 rib centerlines in thoracic CT is essential for unfolded rib visualization, fracture detection, and surgical navigation, but remains challenging due to adjacent-bone confluence, calcified costal cartilage bridges, kyphotic pose variation, and partial visibility of terminal ribs. We present ribline, an open-source three-stage framework combining: (1) an automatically detected lung-apex and vertebral-midline coordinate frame with a kyphosis-aware azimuthal angle for point ordering along each rib; (2) a hybrid voxel detector fusing an anatomically anchored Semantic Context Forest (SCF) with a lightweight 3D U-Net; and (3) a global stage that decomposes the probability skeleton into candidate curves, assigns rib indices via a bilateral Viterbi dynamic program coupled across both hemithoraces, and refines curves via template recovery and normal-plane centering (RibSnake). On the Siemens Corporate Research 2 mm thoracic CT benchmark (47 training and 12 evaluation scans), our pipeline achieves a labeled Chamfer distance of 2.05 mm, labeled clDice of 0.886 (3 mm) and 0.945 (4 mm), 97.2% labeling accuracy (278/286 ribs), and zero false-positive curves on the evaluation split, and 3.64 mm (median 2.39 mm) with 91.8% labeling accuracy across all 59 annotated scans (1,402 ribs) in 5-fold cross-validation. Code: https://github.com/wq2012/ribline Pretrained Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/wq2012/ribline

entry.title: Jensen-Bregman split Gibbs sampling
entry.summary: Split Gibbs sampling (SGS) is a versatile tool to sample from complex posterior distributions, such as those arising in imaging inverse problems. However, existing SGS instances are limited to quadratic variable couplings, restricting their applicability to Gaussian likelihoods. This letter genearalizes SGS to non-Euclidean geometry by introducing a coupling kernel defined through a Jensen-Bregman divergence. This framework not only enables posterior sampling in these settings but also unifies several \emph{ad hoc} sampling schemes from the literature under a principled theoretical foundation.

entry.title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
entry.summary: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.

entry.title: Efficient Multimodal Beam Prediction for Real-World 6G UAV Communications via Image-Position-Synthetic Fusion
entry.summary: Camera-based beam selection can reduce the need for exhaustive channel measurement in highly mobile millimeter-wave UAV links, but the complementary value of visual and position-derived representations and their behavior under modality degradation require further investigation. This paper develops a staged multimodal framework for current-beam prediction using real-world UAV measurements. The proposed 32-beam classifier combines an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B3 visual encoder with two deterministic position-derived representations: an explicit Geometric-Kinematic vector and a nonlinear synthetic feature basis constructed from position. The image and synthetic representations are fused first, followed by late fusion with the geometry representation. Experiments on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23 show that Image-Synthetic fusion achieves 86.92% Top-1, 99.03% Top-3, and 99.56% Top-5 accuracy, improving Top-1 performance by 2.64 percentage points over image-only inference and outperforming the 60.71% Top-1 accuracy of synthetic-only inference. Adding the Geometric-Kinematic branch yields the highest measured performance, reaching 87.14% Top-1, 99.12% Top-3, and 99.60% Top-5 accuracy. Controlled input interventions further demonstrate complementary behavior under visual degradation and strong sensitivity to severe synthetic-input corruption. Position-derived nonlinear features provide complementary information to visual context and improve current-beam prediction in the evaluated real-world UAV setting.

entry.title: A Configurable ETC2 Encoder with Learned Search
entry.summary: ETC2 fixes the texture representation and bit rate, leaving the encoder to trade search time for distortion. We present a configurable CPU encoder in which rules or small neural networks allocate conventional ETC2 searches; these searches construct every encoded block. Configurations span fast-encoder output through broader mode and endpoint searches. On 64 color textures used to evaluate and select configurations, the fastest measured configurations reaching at least Google Etc2Comp's pooled REC709 PSNR at efforts 0-49.5 run 30.7-40.9 times faster. A high-quality configuration exceeds effort-100 PSNR with 64.1% less time. At equal search quotas, learned action ranking and second-search allocation jointly gain 0.124 dB over rule-based choices. At high quality, learning saves time at a small distortion cost. Outputs retain standard ETC2 storage and hardware decoding.

entry.title: A Miniaturized Wi-Fi HaLow-Based Wireless Imaging Transfer System for Capsule Endoscopy
entry.summary: Wireless capsule endoscopy is constrained by severe limitations in size, available power, and reliable data transmission through biological tissues. Although recent advances in miniature imaging sensors have improved image quality, the wireless transmission of color images at practical frame rates remains a challenging task under the tight capsule constraints. We present the design and the experimental validation of a miniaturized Wireless Imaging Transfer (WIT) system for capsule endoscopy based on a sub-GHz IEEE 802.11ah (Wi-Fi HaLow) wireless link. In addition, a preliminary in-vivo validation of Wi-Fi HaLow communication is reported, showing that a stable through-body wireless link can be established across biological tissues in a clinically relevant porcine model. These in-vivo results provide direct experimental support for the adoption of sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow for capsule endoscopy applications. Experimental results demonstrate stable wireless image transmission at a resolution of 320x320 pixels, with measured end-to-end data rates above 12 Mbps and a transmission energy efficiency of 20.7 nJ/bit. We also report a detailed power consumption analysis, with a breakdown of the contributions from the imaging sensor, illumination, digital processing, and RF transmission. When all active subsystem contributions are considered, including the camera, digital processing, RF transmission, and illumination at 60% LED brightness, the total power consumption is approximately 477 mW, corresponding to a complete-chain energy consumption of approximately 39.6 nJ/bit. Overall, the measured performance confirms that sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow provides a promising trade-off among throughput, robustness, and energy efficiency for wireless imaging in capsule endoscopy.

entry.title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification
entry.summary: Gate coefficients describe how a fusion layer weights intermediate features, but they do not necessarily reflect the magnitude of branch contributions at the classifier output. We investigate this distinction in a fixed 3D MedVAE--radiomics model for clear cell versus non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from contrast-enhanced CT. Because the model uses a linear classification head, the binary decision logit can be decomposed exactly into a gated image term, a direct radiomics term, and a bias. We define effective radiomics dominance as the direct radiomics term's share of the summed absolute non-bias branch contributions and compare it with structural radiomics weighting. Internally, mean structural radiomics weighting was 0.823, whereas mean effective radiomics dominance was 0.148, with a modest case-wise association (\r{ho} = 0.290). The gated image term retained substantially stronger discriminative ranking information than the direct radiomics term. The same structural-to-effective discrepancy was observed in exploratory external evaluation. Branch-targeted permutation, integrated-gradient, and Shapley-style analyses further identified radiomics descriptors influencing the direct radiomics term. Because radiomics also generates the gate, the gated image term remains radiomics-dependent, so additive branch contribution should not be interpreted as total input influence. These findings show that structural gate weighting and decision-level branch contribution represent distinct aspects of gated feature fusion and should be interpreted separately.

entry.title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
entry.summary: Reliable probability estimates are important for the clinical interpretation of machine-learning classifiers, yet radiomics--image fusion models for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) are commonly evaluated primarily by discrimination. Using 396 patients from the KiTS23 dataset, we evaluated whether adding radiomics to four image-model families improved probabilistic performance in addition to discrimination. Seventeen individual models and four probability-average ensembles were assessed using discrimination, probability calibration, and proper scoring measures. Across 12 matched image-only versus fusion comparisons, AUC and AP improved in all 12, while Brier score and negative log likelihood (NLL) improved in 11 of 12 and expected calibration error (ECE) in eight of 12. The 3D MedVAE gated-fusion model achieved the strongest overall individual-model profile. Probability averaging across concatenation, cross-attention, and gated fusion produced favourable point estimates across all five primary metrics relative to image-only models in all four families, although paired-bootstrap support was stronger for Brier score and NLL than for ECE. These findings show that radiomics--image fusion can improve probabilistic prediction quality beyond discrimination, while calibration behaviour varies across image architectures and fusion strategies. We show that our proposed probability-average ensemble models improve discrimination and calibration simultaneously across all architectures in the study.

entry.title: C$^2$LUE: Clinically Aligned Patient-Level Ultrasound Diagnosis via Evidence-Aware Multi-Instance Learning
entry.summary: Patient-level ultrasound diagnosis demands not only high predictive accuracy but also clinically aligned mitigation of asymmetric diagnostic risks. While Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) effectively models routine multi-view exams, standard aggregators often dilute heterogeneous diagnostic cues and optimize solely for global accuracy. This frequently yields undesirable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs. To bridge this gap, we propose C$^2$LUE, a novel MIL framework coupling evidence aware aggregation with risk-aligned regularization. To preserve evidence heterogeneity and prevent unimodal attention collapse, C$^2$LUE employs a multi-query cross-attention mechanism built upon a LoRA-adapted DINOv3 backbone. Multiple latent queries explicitly extract and disentangle diverse morphological patterns from the ultrasound sequence. Furthermore, to improve clinical risk alignment, we introduce a dynamic trade-off regularization objective that penalizes sensitivity-specificity imbalance during training. Rather than leaving the clinical trade-off entirely to post-hoc threshold adjustment, this objective encourages the learned score distribution toward a more balanced operating region. Extensive evaluations on patient-level, biopsy-proven thyroid and breast ultrasound datasets demonstrate that C$^2$LUE consistently outperforms prior alternatives. By uniting strong discrimination with a balanced error profile, C$^2$LUE provides a promising solution for real-world ultrasound screening and diagnosis.

entry.title: Can Multimodal Decision Models Classify Breast Ultrasound Images? Benchmarking CLEF and CLEF-Flash Across Prompts and Datasets
entry.summary: Multimodal decision models return probabilities over predefined alternatives, offering a structured interface for image classification. This study benchmarks inference with CLEF and CLEF-Flash on 2818 breast ultrasound images from Dataset B, BUSI, and BUS-BRA. Dataset B and BUS-BRA use binary benign-malignant classification, whereas BUSI includes normal, benign, and malignant categories. Model parameters remain unchanged, and original images are submitted without user-defined preprocessing. Three prompts provide minimal labels, an explicit classification task, or sonographic criteria. We report accuracy, macro F1, balanced accuracy, macro precision, throughput, and latency. CLEF-Flash with the clinical prompt achieves the highest accuracy on all three datasets: 74.85% on Dataset B, 66.28% on BUSI, and 51.63% on BUS-BRA. On BUSI, however, CLEF with the task-guided prompt achieves the highest macro F1 (64.51%) and balanced accuracy (68.72%). CLEF-Flash has lower latency in every matched comparison. Clinical instructions improve CLEF-Flash accuracy relative to the minimal prompt but reduce CLEF accuracy on all datasets. Confusion matrices reveal frequent benign-to-malignant errors, particularly on BUS-BRA, where all configurations fall below the 67.63% accuracy of a majority-class predictor. These findings demonstrate dataset-and prompt-dependent performance and motivate class-specific evaluation before applying multimodal decision models to breast ultrasound analysis.

entry.title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI
entry.summary: Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.

entry.title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data
entry.summary: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

entry.title: Exploring the Latent Structure of AMD Severity Using Retinal Foundation Models
entry.summary: Retinal foundation models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, yet relatively little is known about how disease-related information is represented within their learned embeddings and whether this distribution influences downstream prediction performance. In this work, we use Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) as a case study to investigate how disease severity is represented within the embedding space of RET-CLIP, a retinal vision-language foundation model, using bilateral fundus images from the AREDS dataset, benchmarked against non-retinal encoders. We first characterize the distribution of AMD severity within the learned representation space and then evaluate how this structure influences classification performance across three clinically relevant task formulations of increasing granularity. Finally, we analyze the most influential latent dimensions combining feature attribution, statistical phenotype association, and qualitative image analyses. Our results show that RET-CLIP represents AMD severity as a continuous spectrum rather than a set of discrete categories, with healthy and advanced disease stages exhibiting clearer separation than intermediate ones. This organization was reflected in downstream performance, which decreased from a balanced accuracy of 0.844 and 0.814 for binary AMD and Late-AMD detection respectively to 0.446 for six-class grading. Furthermore, the most influential latent dimensions were statistically associated to distinct retinal phenotypes, including drusen accumulation, pigmentary alterations, and advanced retinal lesions. These findings suggest that the structure of retinal foundation-model representations influences the difficulty of clinically relevant prediction tasks and demonstrate the potential of representation-level analysis for understanding disease organization and improving interpretability.

entry.title: Desertification Forecasting in Semi-Arid Regions: Using Deep Learning to Probe the Observability Limits of Land Degradation Dynamics
entry.summary: Forecasting desertification has received far less attention than mapping it. We use a convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) trained on ten annual Earth Observation (EO) variables (2000-2023) over the semi-arid state of Ceará, Brazil, on a 256x206 grid at roughly 2.2 km resolution, to measure how much of the year-to-year evolution of a MapBiomas-derived degradation index (IDV) can be predicted from satellite data. The network predicts a bounded change on top of the last observed state, is trained in two stages (single-step, then recursive rollout) and is evaluated on a contiguous spatial and temporal holdout. State-wide mean IDV rose from 0.238 to 0.350 between 2000 and 2023, about 0.005 per year, but cell-level change is dominated by year-to-year jumps, and a gradient-boosting model given all channels explains only 4.7% of its variance. Against this ceiling, the ConvLSTM lowers RMSE relative to persistence by 1.6% one year ahead and 4.4% four years ahead in a held-out southern band (p < 0.001), beats persistence with a constant drift and reproduces 53-69% of the regional drift. Drift-aware baselines only help from the third year onward, by up to 4.4% in RMSE at six years. An earlier formulation that redrew the whole field each year predicted changes unrelated to the observed ones (correlation -0.06) and produced a spurious decline when run recursively. Channel knockouts suggest that elevation and EVI degrade the forecast, while slope and aspect have no measurable effect. Monte Carlo dropout and stochastic scenario maps convey the uncertainty that the expected-value forecast hides. Under climatological forcing, mean IDV rises from 0.350 in 2023 to 0.370 in 2030. EO-based desertification forecasting is therefore reliable for the regional trend, not for individual cells.

entry.title: Radiomics-Based Thyroid Nodule Classification with Label-Conditional Conformal Prediction
entry.summary: Thyroid nodule malignancy assessment relies on ultrasound imaging, yet current risk stratification systems suffer from substantial interobserver variability, contributing to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies. We propose a radiomics-based framework combining quantitative feature extraction via PyRadiomics with a Generalized Additive Model (GAM) classifier, selected among six candidates for its favorable trade-off between discriminative performance and interpretability. To complement point predictions with uncertainty estimates, Cross-Conformal Prediction with label-conditional guarantees is applied, flagging ambiguous cases for clinical review rather than forcing a binary decision. Experiments are conducted on TN5000, a publicly available ultrasound dataset of thyroid nodules. After Spearman correlation filtering, 36 features are retained and the GAM achieves an AUC of $0.89$, a sensitivity of $0.83$, and a specificity of $0.82$ on the validation set. At a significance level $ε=0.09$, selected to ensure empirical coverage guarantees on both classes, 63\% of nodules on the test set receive a certain (i.e., single-label) prediction, with conditional precision of $0.94$ for certain malignant and conditional Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of $0.73$ for certain benign cases, while the remaining 37\% are referred to the clinician.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining on Multi-Domain Raman Spectra
entry.summary: Raman spectroscopy generates large volumes of unlabeled data that are difficult to exploit with conventional supervised learning. This work introduces a multi-domain self-supervised learning framework based on a masked autoencoder (MAE) for learning transferable Raman spectral representations from heterogeneous biological, chemical, forensic, and materials datasets. The proposed pretraining strategy incorporates physics-aware objectives by combining masked intensity reconstruction with a sparse Voigt-profile decoder that models spectral peak structure through differentiable peak centers, widths, and amplitudes. A denoising objective is further included to improve robustness to spectral corruption. The learned encoder is evaluated on substance classification, component identification, concentration estimation, and spectral denoising under linear probing, attention-based probing, end-to-end fine-tuning, and training from scratch. Experimental results show that self-supervised pretraining is most beneficial for challenging tasks with limited labeled data. Attention-based probing also reveals substantially more useful information in the frozen representation than linear probing, indicating that conventional linear evaluation may underestimate representation quality. In addition, the benefits of pretraining become more pronounced with increasing encoder capacity. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates that physics-aware, multi-domain self-supervised pretraining can improve label efficiency, robustness, and transferability across diverse Raman spectroscopy tasks.

entry.title: The Predictability Bias of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Medical Imaging
entry.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias. In computed tomography (CT), recurrent anatomy is predictable from context, whereas the sporadic, localized pathology that determines clinical interpretation often is not. We introduce TAP-JEPA, a ViT-B/3D trained on 113,611 CT volumes that is competitive with state-of-the-art encoders (COLIPRI, Merlin, VoxelFM) in scan-level classification. We then audit the learned predictive pathway by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations used during training. Prediction lowers the mean Skill (prevalence-normalized average precision) from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology, but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy. Along the teacher direction, separating pathology from matched control regions in the same organ, prediction moves pathology 34.7% toward the controls and controls 13.6% toward pathology, with larger shifts farther from visible context. Replacing visible matched-control representations increases surrounding-target prediction loss more than fully replacing pathology representations across four pathology categories. Downstream, removing all final-layer pathology tokens reduces the decision margin by at most 0.45% in four of seven scan-level probes. Together, these results show that contextual predictability is not a sufficient proxy for clinical relevance in medical representation learning. Training objectives should therefore retain diagnostic features regardless of their predictability from surrounding anatomy.

entry.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
entry.summary: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.

entry.title: Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model for Vessel Extraction Using Physics-informed Synthetic Data
entry.summary: Accurate artery extraction from X-ray coronary angiography (XCA) is essential for coronary artery disease diagnosis and intervention. However, low vessel visibility, respiratory and cardiac motion, and limited annotations challenge existing methods. Moreover, most deep learning approaches produce binary vessel masks without preserving clinically relevant intra-arterial contrast information. We propose a Temporal Diffusion Bridge Model (TDBM) that formulates vessel extraction as image translation and learns from physics-informed synthetic data without manual vessel annotations. A physics-based XCA synthesis engine generates diverse, perfectly aligned pairs of contrast-enhanced and contrast-free images. Using these pairs, TDBM learns cross-domain mappings to recover high-fidelity vessel information. Temporal conditioning incorporates adjacent frames to improve consistency, while a vessel-aware contrastive loss exploits background-invariant synthetic pairs to enhance vascular discrimination. We evaluate TDBM on two XCA vessel segmentation datasets and conduct a reader study using two real-patient XCA sequence datasets. Zero-shot segmentation is further assessed on retinal imaging and fluorescence microscopy datasets. Results demonstrate that TDBM consistently outperforms existing methods and generalizes effectively across imaging modalities. Code and trained weights will be available at: https://github.com/Advanced-AI-in-Medicine-and-Physics-Lab/TDBM

entry.title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
entry.summary: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.

entry.title: Ultrasound and Magnetic Resonance Elastography of the Neck: Biomechanical Basis, Clinical Applications and Methodological Challenges
entry.summary: Many neck disorders, from chronic neck pain and headache to thyroid and nodal malignancy and radiation-induced fibrosis, both arise from and alter the mechanical properties of neck tissues, yet clinical assessment still relies on morphology, palpation and symptoms. Ultrasound and magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) now allow these properties to be measured in vivo, but the neck literature differs widely in methodology and remains dispersed across modalities and tissues. This review brings together the biomechanical basis of neck tissue behavior, the clinical conditions that alter it, and the principles and applications of ultrasound elastography and MRE in the neck. We show that ultrasound elastography has demonstrated diagnostic value for thyroid nodules and cervical lymph nodes, while neck MRE has been shown to be feasible but remains at an early stage. Across both modalities, reported values depend strongly on fiber orientation, posture, muscle activation and acquisition conditions. We therefore propose reporting recommendations and discuss how measurements beyond stiffness, including anisotropy, viscosity and nonlinearity, could improve disease management and inform computational models of the neck.

entry.title: When pose graphs are not enough: a failure analysis of pose-graph-based camera estimation for Gaussian splatting
entry.summary: Exterior Gaussian-splat twins for real-estate listings are captured to a fixed recipe: a consumer drone orbits a single property in several overlapping passes at stepped altitudes, with occasional vertical ascents, so the imagery is dense, sequential, GPS- and time-tagged, and revisits each facade from many angles. This structure is tantalizing: it suggests camera poses could be recovered by a dense pose-graph optimization (PGO) whose only unknowns are the poses, far fewer than the joint pose-and-point problem bundle adjustment (BA) solves. PGO is mature in robotics, but almost always as post-processing: it redistributes the drift of an already-decent trajectory once loop closures tie it together. Splatting captures push that regime to its limit, every frame closing loops with dozens of others, raising a clean question: does pose-only optimization reach BA accuracy? We built a system specialized to this capture structure, not a general-purpose SfM tool, to test it. It beat COLMAP on speed but never on quality; this paper is the candid post-mortem. The shortfall arises from several interacting causes, hand-set weights, greedy merging and a noisy GPS ruler, together with two limits inherent to the formulation: SE(3) edges carry no scale degree of freedom, so independently scaled sub-maps drift when merged, and a two-view edge stops short of the coupling one 3D point imposes on every frame that sees it. A viable design must add back Sim(3) constraints, absolute GPS priors, retained structure, and uncertainty-aware weighting

entry.title: LVS: Local View Synthesis from Relative Camera Pose by Reusing Previous Views
entry.summary: Interactive scene exploration requires frequent view updates, although small camera motions preserve much of the visible content. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting nevertheless renders each target view, leaving this image overlap unexploited. Reusing rendered images offers an alternative. Geometric warping alone cannot recover newly exposed content and remains sensitive to depth errors. We propose a per-scene framework that replaces repeated scene rendering for nearby views with relative-pose-guided RGB-D image reuse. Geometric warping uses depth and relative pose to transport source content, while a lightweight multiscale network predicts RGB residuals to correct artifacts and infer missing appearance. Cached source features further reduce repeated computation. On GS-render, residual refinement improves PSNR by 0.72~dB over pure warping; evaluations on captured and rendered scenes demonstrate low query latency. This separation of scene rendering from local view updates supports responsive scene exploration, with potential applications in augmented and virtual reality.

entry.title: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization via Complex-Valued Fusion
entry.summary: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization (OV-AVEL) labels each video segment with an event class, including classes that were never seen during training. The dominant pipeline uses a frozen multimodal foundation model (e.g. ImageBind) to embed the visual frame, the audio mel-spectrogram, and each candidate class name into a shared space, then computes two cosine similarities for each segment against each class: visual-text and audio-text. Existing methods then collapse this pair into a single scalar score with a fixed rule (geometric mean, weighted average) before taking the argmax. Instead, we compute complex-valued similarities and learn their fusion using a complex-valued neural network (CVNN). Each modality's standard representation becomes the real part of our pipeline, and a paired companion stream supplies the imaginary part. We use imaginary part of iHSV for visual modality and CycleGAN-translated phase spectrogram for audio modality as these companion streams. This results in two complex similarities, which are then fused. While the vision and audio encoders remain frozen, only the temporal-attention blocks and the fusion CVNN are trained. The four-stream complex architecture sets a new state of the art on both OV-AVEL benchmarks. On the open (unseen-class) split of OV-AVEBench we reach 66.5/59.1/54.1% Acc/Seg-F1/Event-F1 (+1.6/+4.1/+6.6 over the previously reported fine-tuned baseline), with consistent gains for seen classes as well. We also modify AVE dataset for this task and observe that our architecture reaches 60.7/51.9/50.4% Acc/Seg-F1/Event-F1, achieving state-of-the-art OV-AVEL results on it as well. We also propose a two-stream alternative, which also sees great improvements over the baseline.

entry.title: Localization of Candidate Kikuchi Regions in RHEED Images: Visibility and Annotation Boundaries
entry.summary: Kikuchi lines and bands in reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) carry information on crystal geometry and electron scattering, but are often obscured by intense diffraction streaks. We combine multiscale convolution with spatial detail from skip connections and independent supervision that allows overlapping regions to localize streaks and candidate Kikuchi regions separately. Using manual polygon annotations made before model-assisted editing, the Kikuchi intersection-over-union (IoU) on 29 laboratory test images from separate growth batches was $0.6290 \pm 0.0137$. We then performed supervised adaptation to public chalcogenide images and stratified images by Kikuchi visibility using the median ratings of three observers who rated the images separately, two of whom rated with predictions hidden. With all 244 training images, IoU for the clear-feature group of 10 test images was $0.5014 \pm 0.0336$, whereas ambiguous images gave lower values. With 100 training images, clear-group IoU was $0.5171 \pm 0.0073$; expanding the training set also reduced responses on images without target features. Reported uncertainties are sample standard deviations across four laboratory runs or three adaptation runs. Public-image adaptation used reference masks of mixed provenance, including prediction-derived drafts. The method converts visual cues into inspectable spatial regions, providing a basis for analysis of line positions, intersections, and local intensity.

entry.title: A Unified Score Matching Paradigm for Video Anomaly Detection and Anticipation
entry.summary: Video anomaly detection (VAD) is a fundamental and safety-critical task in computer vision. Recent generative approaches detect anomalies from a distributional perspective, but remain limited by local anomaly modes. Meanwhile, video anomaly anticipation (VAA), as a proactive extension beyond post-hoc detection, introduces additional challenges. In particular, the contrastive inference paradigm in VAD, which relies on ground-truth frames, is not applicable to VAA, hindering its development. To address these challenges, we propose a unified score-driven framework, termed Uni-DSM, based on denoising score matching (DSM), which models anomaly patterns through likelihood estimation and score functions over the learned data distribution. Within this unified framework, we adopt a shared noise-conditioned score transformer backbone with scene-dependent embeddings and motion-aware weighting for distribution-level modeling. Instead of introducing separate architectures, Uni-DSM unifies VAD and VAA through different inference and supervision paradigms built upon the same score-based formulation. For VAD, we instantiate an autoregressive denoising score matching (ADSM) mechanism, which progressively accumulates anomalous evidence via autoregressive denoising, enabling enhanced perception of local modes beyond visual cues. For VAA, we extend the same architecture by incorporating a lightweight auxiliary decoder and a novel self-distilled denoising score matching (SDSM) mechanism. By constructing supervision from output discrepancies instead of relying on unavailable future ground truth, our method achieves efficient training suitable or early anomaly anticipation. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both VAD and VAA while maintaining high efficiency, establishing a unified and scalable pipeline from anomaly detection to anticipation.

entry.title: Improving Image-Based Nutrition Estimation Through Multimodal Food-Item Verification and Recovery
entry.summary: Single-image nutrition estimation can fail silently when visible foods are missed. Even when a food is correctly identified, its proposed region may not support portion estimation. We propose a framework that uses multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to inventory visible foods and separately verify food identity and whether each proposed 2D region supports portion estimation. One whole-image review uses these verification results to identify unresolved gaps and omitted foods, triggering at most one targeted recovery pass. Recovered regions are re-verified without access to the recovery prompt, then reconciled into a final item set for nutrition estimation. The framework requires no task-specific fine-tuning. Matched evaluation on common valid-output samples shows that item-level grounding improves mass accuracy across all tested settings and energy accuracy relative to an adapted retrieval baseline, with item-identity precision and recall also improving, while post-recovery visual coverage is assessed separately at inference time without ground-truth annotations.

entry.title: Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation for Thin Curvilinear Structures
entry.summary: Accurate segmentation of thin curvilinear structures is vital for various real-world applications, from vessel analysis to road extraction. Yet their intricate geometry makes even minor pixel-wise errors enough to break the global topology, and this structural fragility turns severe domain shifts into catastrophic failures. The difficulty is most acute under cross-modality gaps, where the imaging process itself differs fundamentally between source and target. While test-time adaptation (TTA) offers a practical source-free remedy, existing methods adapt feature statistics and confidence, neither of which constrains connectivity, and thus degrade under such extreme gaps. To address this, we propose Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation (SGP-TTA). Progressive Batch Normalization (ProgBN) shifts normalization from frozen source statistics toward current target estimates under a sample-count schedule, so that the source-target balance follows the stage of adaptation rather than a fixed coefficient. Consensus Skeleton Recall (CSR) then derives a structural target from geometrically aligned multi-view predictions and updates only the BN affine parameters to preserve connected structures. Extensive experiments show that SGP-TTA consistently outperforms existing TTA methods in topological connectivity, with the largest margins under cross-modality shift. The project page is available at https://boa-jang.github.io/SGP-TTA.

entry.title: Adapting Appearance-Based Gaze Estimation to Narrow-Range, Long-Duration Screen Viewing
entry.summary: Appearance-based gaze estimation offers a low-cost alternative to infrared eye tracking for screen-based behavioral and clinical applications, however existing models are typically developed for wide ranges of gaze angle and head pose. Prolonged screen viewing presents a distinct regime in which gaze remains near the screen center, head motion is limited, and calibration drift accumulates over time. In this work, we benchmark six published estimators along with a proposed differential-gaze model on 140 long-duration facial video recordings with synchronized eye tracking under subject-disjoint evaluation and a common budget of calibration frames. Differential estimation was the only static method that significantly improved upon a baseline predictor of each recording's mean gaze, and was further boosted by addition of temporal context. It also yielded the strongest agreement with reference fixations and saccades, demonstrating that low angular error alone could not validate eye movement reconstruction. These findings establish differential estimation as a promising foundation for reliable gaze tracking in long-duration, narrow-range settings.

entry.title: CrossEdit: Cross-Modal Training Enables Rich Audio-Visual Editing
entry.summary: Multimedia editing requires generative models to interpret complex, compositional instructions and modify only the desired elements across modalities, a capability largely beyond existing systems. Current approaches are typically limited to simple, single-attribute edits within one modality, since diverse, high-quality editing pairs are hard to obtain, especially for cross-modal tasks where aligned audiovisual (AV) data is scarce. We present CrossEdit, a unified omni-modal editing model for images, audio, and video that performs AV movie scene edits zero-shot through cross-modal transfer. Our key observation is that complex instruction-following, once learned in any modality, generalizes to others. We exploit the additive nature of acoustic signals to procedurally generate large-scale audio editing pairs with compositional instructions, and show that fine-tuning on this synthetic data and self-supervised AV masked reconstruction, alongside a targeted set of curated cross-modal tasks, induces instruction-following that transfers zero-shot to unseen modality and instruction combinations. To evaluate this capability, we release CrossEditBench, a human-annotated benchmark of AV edits on movie scenes, and propose AV-FES, a metric that jointly scores instruction following and consistency. We show that our proposed techniques improve performance on zero-shot AV movie scene editing, while maintaining or improving performance on lip-synced speech editing and standard image, video, and audio editing benchmarks. Demos are available at https://wanchichen.github.io/crossedit/.

entry.title: Diagnosing Diversity Collapse and Validating Mask-Conditioned Diffusion for Labeled Microtubule Microscopy
entry.summary: Mask-conditioned diffusion models have become standard for generating labeled training data in biomedical imaging. But the tools used to evaluate them were built for a different problem. Standard metrics like FID and KID score images through ImageNet-trained features. Those features do not transfer to microscopy, leaving the metrics poorly calibrated for specialized domains. Even with a domain-appropriate feature space, a single blended number can still hide a real failure: a model can produce visually plausible images that still transfer poorly to downstream tasks. We identify a specific failure mode: Late in training, realism keeps improving while texture diversity collapses. The model settles onto a fixed color palette, converging to a high-similarity, low-diversity state that standard metrics do not penalize. Therefore, we propose a diversity-aware diagnostic in a domain-validated feature space. It combines a realism axis based on inter-similarity to real images with a diversity axis based on intra-similarity among generated samples. This diagnostic selects a checkpoint that domain experts cannot reliably distinguish from real recordings in a forced-choice study. It also yields useful downstream segmentation: a segmenter trained only on synthetically labeled data reaches a median skeletonised IoU comparable to one trained on real data, at lower cross-fold variance, and clearly ahead of the best available public alternative in this domain, a parametric renderer. We also reproduce a data-efficient hyperparameter-transfer experiment from prior work, tuning several foundation segmenters on a small labeled subset and evaluating on real images: transfer is stronger with our data. We release DiffuMT on HuggingFace, including the triplet dataset, code to reproduce the downstream-utility validation, and a standalone diagnostic tool for evaluating mask-conditioned diffusion models.

entry.title: Entity-Aware Evaluation of OCR Systems for Historical Document Transcription
entry.summary: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) is essential for digitizing historical archives, yet standard evaluation metrics such as Character Error Rate (CER) do not necessarily reflect whether meaningful information, such as names, dates, and identifiers, is preserved. In this work, we investigate entitylevel analysis of OCR errors as a complementary perspective for evaluating OCR quality in historical documents. Using a publicly available benchmark of 175 documents from the Berrutti Archive, augmented with 5,209 manually annotated entity mentions that will be released upon acceptance, we compare sequence-recognition OCR systems, OCR-specialized vision-language models, and general-purpose vision-language models. Beyond global transcription accuracy, we analyze entity preservation and recoverability under varying character-level edit tolerances. Our experiments show that OCR rankings depend on the evaluation criterion: while Qwen 3.6 achieves the highest entity coverage across all tested tolerances, several systems with lower exact-match coverage recover substantially when small errors are tolerated, suggesting that many of their errors correspond to localized character-level deviations rather than fundamentally incorrect entity transcriptions. Conversely, some systems remain unable to recover many entities even under relaxed matching. These findings show that OCR quality cannot be fully characterized by aggregate transcription metrics alone and highlight the importance of evaluating how OCR errors affect the preservation and recoverability of meaningful information.

entry.title: On-Device Super-Resolution Imaging for a Low-Cost SPAD Array on a 640-KB-SRAM Microcontroller
entry.summary: This work presents a super-resolution (SR) deep-learning (DL) architecture to simultaneously upscale low-resolution (LR) depth and intensity images acquired by a consumer-grade VL53L9CX time-of-flight (ToF) sensor, a compact single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) ranging device, while targeting deployment on a resource-constrained microcontroller (MCU) with only 640 KB SRAM and 2 MB Flash. The VL53L9CX provides 54 $\times$ 42 depth and intensity measurements. The proposed framework performs $\times$4 spatial SR to reconstruct 216 $\times$ 168 depth and intensity images simultaneously. The network employs separate reconstruction branches for intensity and high-resolution (HR) depth. We train the network with efficient loss functions and investigate the performance by testing multiple compact, hardware-oriented backbones, including Spatially Adaptive Feature Modulation (SAFM), Swift Parameter-Free Attention Network (SPAN), and Residual Local Feature Network (RLFN). We evaluate the network on both synthetic and real measurements, with particular attention to constrained activation and memory storage. We export the selected network to ONNX, quantize it to INT8, generate C inference code for an STM32H563ZI Arm Cortex-M33 MCU, and integrate it with our simplified sensor's firmware. This work is the first to demonstrate a compact DL SR model on a low-cost bare-metal MCU for a consumer-grade LR SPAD sensor, integrated with customized MCU firmware to enable on-device SR inference.

entry.title: Hybrid++: The Bridge between PDE Models and Deep Learning for Gamma Noise Removal
entry.summary: Multiplicative gamma noise is one of the dominant noise factors in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and medical ultrasound images. They are dependent on pixel level noises due to which they are highly varying across the image and harder to handle as compared to additive noise. The denoising methods to address this noise currently include classical partial differential equation (PDE) methods which are good for interpretation but lack the restoration ability as compared to the state-of-the-art models while deep convolutional networks like DnCNN achieve high performance but at the cost of transparency due to which practitioners are skeptical to use them in high-risk critical fields like medicine. This paper presents Hybrid++, a novel trainable nonlinear reaction-diffusion architecture that addresses both the concerns - staying interpretable while offering performance close to huge black-box models. It combines a fully learnable PDE initialization with a 3-stage reaction-diffusion network having 64-channel multiscale filter banks, 4-layer Squeeze-and-Excitation attention-based influence functions and a 64-dimensional noise level embedding. It uses a two-phase training strategy, stage-wise optimization followed by joint end-to-end refinement which enables co-adaptation of all learnable parameters. On the FoE benchmark, Hybrid++ substantially improves over classical PDE, BM3D and the original TNRD baselines. In the severe-noise setting L=1, it comes within 0.23 dB PSNR of a separately trained DnCNN while using only about 8% of its parameters. We therefore position Hybrid++ not as a universal state-of-the-art image restoration backbone, but as a compact, physically structured reaction-diffusion model for multiplicative gamma noise.

entry.title: RACE-FPP: A Robust AI-assisted Characterisation Enhancement for Fringe Projection Profilometry
entry.summary: Fringe Projection Profilometry (FPP) requires precise system characterisation to achieve reliable three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions; however, characterisation accuracy strongly depends on robust checkerboard feature localisation, which can deteriorate under challenging imaging conditions such as lens blur and characterisation target orientations. Existing deep learning-based corner detectors are typically assessed using detection metrics and camera reprojection error alone, without considering their wider impact on projector characterisation, camera-projector stereo characterisation consistency, or overall measurement accuracy. In this work, we introduce a complete FPP characterisation pipeline that incorporates deep learning-based corner detection into the standard camera characterisation workflow. We also characterise the projector by sampling phase values at the centres of the white squares in the characterisation target. Rather than treating corner detection as an isolated task, the proposed framework explicitly analyses how localisation errors propagate throughout the entire FPP characterisation chain. Performance is evaluated using detection metrics (e.g., precision and recall), camera and projector reprojection errors, and the camera and projector stereo characterisation. Across a mixed dataset of clean and degraded images, the camera reprojection error is reduced from 1.237 pixels to 0.259 pixels, while the projector reprojection error is reduced by roughly 50%. Dimensional evaluation of reconstructed artefacts shows improved geometric accuracy compared with those resulting from the conventional pipeline. Overall, the findings indicate increased robustness of system-level characterisation under challenging imaging conditions, thereby enabling more reliable industrial FPP measurements.

entry.title: Laplace-Domain Beamforming for Ultrafast Plane-Wave Imaging
entry.summary: Fourier-domain beamforming methods, such as filtered backpropagation (FBP), are beneficial in ultrafast plane-wave imaging due to their computational efficiency and high image quality. These methods use the Fourier diffraction theorem (FDT) for steered plane waves to exactly invert linear scattering models. However, these models rely on simplifying assumptions that degrade image quality. The use of linear transducer arrays, in particular, requires: (i) a two-dimensional space, and (ii) lossless tissues. Herein, Laplace-domain beamforming is proposed. This method retains the computational efficiency of the Fourier-domain methods while improving image quality for linear arrays. Specifically, the method uses a generalization of the FDT, here called Laplace diffraction theorem, to account for three spatial dimensions, finite array element heights, and lossy tissues. A phantom experiment showed that the proposed method improves image uniformity, spatial resolution, and contrast compared to FBP. Using three steering angles, the lateral and axial -6 dB-widths of wires reduced by up to 12% and 25%, respectively, while the contrast of anechoic regions improved by up to 9%.
